questions.stem: Pale nuclei on the control and all patient slides most strongly suggest:
questions.explanation: A widespread nuclear-staining failure points to hematoxylin strength, time, differentiation, or bluing rather than one specimen.

questions.stem: Milky slides after coverslipping most often result from:

choices.text: Water remaining before xylene or mounting

questions.explanation: Residual water is incompatible with nonaqueous clearing and mounting media and produces cloudiness.

questions.stem: Weak eosin staining is best investigated by reviewing:

choices.text: Eosin pH, concentration, time, and alcohol carryover

questions.explanation: Eosin performance depends on reagent strength and pH, staining time, and subsequent differentiation in alcohol.

questions.stem: The mordant in an alum hematoxylin solution helps:

choices.text: Bind the dye complex to tissue nuclei

questions.explanation: A mordant forms a dye-metal complex that binds nuclear chromatin.

questions.stem: PAS with and without diastase is used to demonstrate:
questions.explanation: Diastase removes glycogen; comparing digested and undigested sections confirms glycogen-dependent PAS positivity.

questions.stem: The preferred positive control for an organism stain is:

choices.text: Tissue known to contain the target organism or structure

questions.explanation: A known positive tissue confirms that the complete staining system can demonstrate the intended target.

questions.stem: A positive control fails for a special stain while the patient tissue is negative. The patient result is:
questions.explanation: A failed positive control means the staining run cannot support interpretation of a negative test slide.
The Prussian blue reaction demonstrates ferric iron, commonly in hemosiderin.

questions.stem: Congo red-stained amyloid is confirmed by:
questions.explanation: Properly stained amyloid demonstrates characteristic apple-green birefringence with polarized light.

questions.stem: The most important purpose of a positive IHC control is to show that:

choices.text: The assay can detect the target under the run conditions
Every test case must be positive
The primary antibody can be omitted

questions.explanation: A known positive control verifies the performance of the assay reagents and procedure.
